I saved the list as `small_intestine_147328` (43 types), and it validated with no warnings. You can load it in Markers… → load a list… and click Annotate. I used marker sets I already know and did not search the literature.

1. **Added:** Paneth cells (ITLN2, ITLN1, SOX9), which the draft dropped because the panel lacks DEFA5/6 and LYZ, so ITLN2 is the key marker here. I also added Enterochromaffin and other enteroendocrine cells (FEV, SLC18A2 / PAX4, SCGN), Eosinophils (CLC, CCR3), two fibroblast types (Telocytes F3/BMP5/SOX6/WNT5A and Trophocytes GREM1/RSPO3/C7/OGN), and Peyer's patch follicular dendritic cells (FDCSP, FCER2).

3. **Removed:** pDC only, because the panel has none of its markers (LILRA4, CLEC4C, IL3RA). The panel can't tell duodenum, jejunum and ileum apart (no FABP6 or SLC10A2), so the list has no types by segment.

| N3 | lamina propria | telocytes, trophocytes, endothelium, CD8 T cells, macrophages | the tissue just under the epithelium (about 26 µm deep), in the villus cores and between crypts |

c08_draw_mucosa.text:
You accepted the outline, and the region `mucosa` is now on the section: one piece with 28,822 cells, about 3.65 mm².

- **How it was drawn:** around the epithelial cells and the telocytes, which are the fibroblasts of the lamina propria, keeping cells within 40 µm of where they are dense. It contains 99% of those cells.
- **What's inside:** 65% epithelial cells, 15% fibroblasts, 8% T and NK cells, plus a little endothelium, myeloid cells and mast cells.
- **Fit to the H&E:** it follows the villi along the top and the crypt bases along the bottom, so the muscle band under the mucosa and the submucosa below stay outside.

Two places to check in the app, where you can reshape the outline with the Regions tools:
- **Left side (tiles J–K, columns 1–6):** a dense patch of immune cells just under the crypts is only partly inside. If it is a lymphoid follicle you want counted as mucosa, extend the region there.
- **Right side (columns 20–24):** the lower edge runs at about row G. Check that it reaches the deepest crypts.

1. **Review candidates:** none of the 7 candidate areas is a real problem. On the H&E each is smooth muscle where it belongs, either muscularis mucosae at the crypt bases or vessel walls in the submucosa, so I dismissed them all. Of the 25 marker checks I kept 4 and dismissed 21: the dismissed ones are panel or biology effects (pan-endothelial genes, mature dendritic cells, vascular smooth muscle among the pericytes) or repeats of a kept problem.
2. **Two pieces of advice kept in the Review panel:** the section needs a colon marker list (it doesn't need new priors). The small-intestine list I drafted for 147328 was used here too, and it produces 4,853 "Paneth cells" (ITLN2 in 0% of them), surface colonocytes called "BEST4+ enterocytes", and no Goblet cells. It also leaves the "Cycling TAs" holding stem cells (745 LGR5+ ASCL2+ cells, while 0 cells are called Stem cells) and goblet cells (RETNLB in 93%); only about 1,250 of the 5,304 really cycle. The Paneth calls contradict COL-05 and your prior U-1.
3. **Context and quality:** the cell types otherwise sit where the colon priors expect: COL-01 (only 17 epithelial cells out of place), COL-06 (plasma cells), COL-11 (neurons) and COL-13 (lymphatics) all hold, and the registration is fine (at most 5.2 µm off). I dropped the advice to draw the mucosa for U-1, because a region would not fix the wrong list, and the advice about epithelial genes spilling into nearby stroma, because no label changes. Nothing in the annotation was changed.

c16_biology.text: Is there anything biologically interesting in these two sections that I should look at?

Yes, several things, though so far only one of the two sections can be trusted. The sigmoid colon (167799) was annotated with the small-intestine list, so its epithelial labels are wrong. The leads below come from gene detection and positions, which don't depend on those labels. Even so, I'd re-annotate the colon with a colon list before reading much into them. Both samples are non-IBD controls from diverticulitis, which frames most of this.

**Sigmoid colon (167799)**

1. **Interferon response in the surface epithelium.** The cells labelled "BEST4+ enterocytes" are really surface colonocytes (3,089 cells). About 66% of them have ISG15 and 60% have IFIT1, against about 4% in the other epithelial cells. That points to an interferon response at the luminal surface, which fits a post-diverticulitis mucosa. Look at ISG15 in the viewer to see whether it is patchy or covers the whole surface.
2. **Signs of injury or repair in the colonocytes.** Part of the wrongly called "Paneth cells" (about 1,500) carry TFF1 and CD177. TFF1 is normally rare in the colon and turns up in regenerating epithelium. Another group (324 cells) has CEACAM8, which is a neutrophil gene, so that could be neutrophils nearby leaking transcripts rather than true epithelial expression. Check both on the H&E.
3. **T cells and dendritic cells deep in the wall.**
   - CD8 T cells sit a median 235 µm from the epithelium, deeper than the usual lamina propria. They gather with B cells and dendritic cells.
   - The dendritic cells (27 cells) are mature, migrating ones (LAMP3, CCR7, IDO1) and gather next to lymphatics.
   - This looks like lymphoid aggregates in the submucosa. That fits the deep, wall-spanning inflammation of diverticulitis.
   - The tiles with many cells of mixed lineage (K11–K14, J7, F16) may be in the same places and are worth a look.
4. **Muscle changes typical of diverticular disease.** Smooth muscle strands run up between the crypts (area A2 from the review), a known change in diverticular disease. The macrophages are mostly LYVE1+ (78%), sit deep in the wall and gather next to neurons, like the resident macrophages of the muscle layers.

**Terminal ileum (147328)**

5. **A possible lymphoid follicle under the crypts.** A dense patch of immune cells sits under the crypts on the left (tiles J–K, columns 1–6). It may be a Peyer's patch or lymphoid follicle. Few B cells or follicular dendritic cells were called there, so either it is mostly T cells, or the B-cell markers detect poorly in this panel. That patch deserves a close-up.
6. **A probable artefact, not biology:** 15% of the cells in the crypt niche are called enterochromaffin cells. That is most likely FEV/SLC18A2 over-calling, not a real expansion.

**Comparing the two sections:** once the colon is re-annotated, comparing ileum and colon from the same disease setting becomes possible. That would cover the fibroblast types (telocytes and trophocytes are called in both) and immune cells in the lamina propria versus the deeper wall.

I can draft and save a colon marker list for 167799 now so you can re-annotate it, then follow up items 1–3 with gene maps and close-ups on the H&E.
